meta.name: SQL Function Sync Validator
meta.description: Validates that SQL functions stored in PostgreSQL (via generated cache from pg_get_functiondef) match the source code tracked in the git repository. Detects DB drift, missing source, signature mismatches, and body differences.

nodes.name: SQL Function Sync Validator
nodes.intent: Detect and report discrepancies between SQL functions in the database (represented by generated cache) and their source code definitions in the repository, so that DB drift is caught before it causes production issues.
constraints: Source of truth is the database (generated cache via pg_get_functiondef)
Must scale to repositories with many schemas
Must gracefully skip unparseable SQL (pglast limitations)
Output must be both human-readable (markdown) and machine-readable (JSON)
nodes.design_notes: Pipeline architecture: Discovery -> Parsing -> Validation -> Reporting. Chosen over a monolithic approach for testability and clear separation of concerns. Parser uses pglast (the official PostgreSQL parser).

history.note: Created IntentGraph by hand as a demonstration.

nodes.name: Discovery
nodes.intent: Locate all SQL function definitions in both the generated cache (database source of truth) and the source code directories, then map each generated function to its source counterpart.
nodes.epistemic_state: known — well-tested discovery with fallback grep
constraints: Generated cache dir: build/db_dump/functions/
Source dirs: sql/functions/ (recursive)
Exclude dirs: sql/functions/deprecated/
Filenames in generated cache follow schema.function_name.sql convention
nodes.design_notes: Three-pass strategy: (1) scan generated cache, (2) scan source dirs, (3) fallback grep for unmatched functions. The fallback grep is optional but catches functions stored in unexpected locations.

nodes.name: Parsing
nodes.intent: Parse SQL function definitions from raw .sql files into structured representations (signature + body), with type normalization to reduce false positives from PostgreSQL's type aliasing.
nodes.epistemic_state: known — uses pglast (official PG parser); robust but has edge cases
constraints: Must use pglast for reliable parsing (not regex-only)
pglast may fail on non-standard SQL (non-SQL procedural languages) — must skip gracefully
Must handle both dollar-quoted and single-quoted function bodies
Must handle multi-statement SQL files
nodes.design_notes: pglast was chosen over regex-only parsing because CREATE FUNCTION syntax is too complex for reliable regex extraction.

nodes.name: Validation
nodes.intent: Compare parsed function representations from the database (generated) against source code, detecting signature mismatches, body differences, and existence gaps, and classify each discrepancy by severity.
nodes.epistemic_state: risky — signature comparison disabled; considering re-enabling with fuzzy matching for v2
constraints: Severity levels: CRITICAL (missing source, signature mismatch), WARNING (body diff), INFO (minor)
Type comparison uses normalized forms (int8 = bigint, etc.)
Body comparison normalizes whitespace before diffing
Parameter type validation currently disabled — not reliable due to OID resolution
nodes.design_notes: Signature validation is intentionally limited: only language is checked as a sanity check. Parameter type and return type comparison was disabled because PostgreSQL's internal type canonicalization and OID resolution in pg_get_functiondef makes exact comparison unreliable.

nodes.name: Reporting
nodes.intent: Generate human-readable and machine-readable reports summarizing validation results, grouped by severity and issue type, with actionable information for each discrepancy.
constraints: Markdown report: VALIDATION_REPORT.md with severity-grouped tables
JSON report: validation_data.json with structured data for tooling
Reports must include pass rate, severity counts, and per-function details
Reports must be generated within seconds for large repositories

nodes.name: Orchestration
nodes.intent: Coordinate the full pipeline: parse CLI arguments, run discovery, iterate through functions for validation, generate reports, and print a summary with appropriate exit code.
constraints: CLI args: --output-dir, --verbose, --skip-fallback-search
Exit code 0 = all valid, exit code 1 = issues found
Must print progress indicators during execution

nodes.name: Generated Cache Scanning
nodes.intent: Scan the generated cache directory for .sql files, parse filenames to extract schema.function_name, and parse each file's SQL to create FunctionRecord entries with generated_parsed data.
constraints: Files named schema.function_name.sql — skip malformed names
Each file contains one CREATE FUNCTION from pg_get_functiondef()

nodes.name: Source Directory Scanning
nodes.intent: Scan all source function directories for .sql files, parse them for CREATE FUNCTION statements (possibly multiple per file), and map each to the corresponding FunctionRecord.
constraints: Multiple functions per file are supported
Excluded directories (sql/functions/deprecated/) are skipped

nodes.name: Fallback Grep Search
nodes.intent: For generated functions with no source match after directory scanning, search the entire repository using grep/ripgrep to find function definitions in unexpected locations.
nodes.epistemic_state: known — optional, can be skipped for speed
constraints: Blacklist approach: exclude only docs/ and deprecated/
10-second timeout per grep search
Falls back to ripgrep if grep is not found
Functions found outside sql/functions/ are flagged

nodes.name: Signature Extraction
nodes.intent: Extract function metadata from pglast AST: schema, name, parameter types, return type, and language.
constraints: Uses pglast AST nodes: CreateFunctionStmt, DefElem, TypeName
Schema defaults to 'public' if not specified
Language defaults to 'plpgsql' if not specified

nodes.name: Body Extraction
nodes.intent: Extract the function body text from a CREATE FUNCTION statement, handling dollar-quoted ($$ ... $$) and single-quoted bodies.
nodes.epistemic_state: constrained — uses heuristic regex, not pure AST
constraints: Must handle $tag$...$tag$ dollar quoting
Must handle '...' single quoting with escaped quotes
Fallback strips LANGUAGE/IMMUTABLE/etc. clauses via regex
nodes.design_notes: Body extraction is regex-based (not from pglast AST) because pglast normalizes the body text, losing the original formatting. We need the raw body for comparison.

nodes.name: Type Normalization
nodes.intent: Normalize PostgreSQL type aliases to canonical forms so that type comparisons are not confused by synonyms (e.g., bigint = int8).
constraints: Canonical forms: int8, int4, int2, float8, float4, bool, bpchar, varchar, text
Also handles: timestamptz, timestamp
Normalization is case-insensitive and whitespace-normalized

nodes.name: Existence Checking
nodes.intent: Detect functions that exist in one location but not the other: in DB but not source (CRITICAL — DB drift), or in source but not DB (WARNING — not deployed).

nodes.name: Signature Comparison
nodes.intent: Compare function signatures between generated and source, currently limited to language-only checking due to type aliasing limitations.
nodes.epistemic_state: constrained — parameter and return type comparison disabled
constraints: Only language is compared (sanity check)
Type validation disabled: PostgreSQL OID resolution makes comparison unreliable

nodes.name: Body Comparison
nodes.intent: Compare function bodies after whitespace normalization, using SequenceMatcher for similarity scoring when bodies differ.
constraints: Whitespace normalized: trailing spaces removed, lines stripped
Uses difflib.SequenceMatcher for similarity ratio
Any difference = WARNING severity

nodes.name: Severity Classification
nodes.intent: Assign severity levels to each discrepancy: CRITICAL for missing source or signature mismatch, WARNING for body differences or unexpected locations, INFO for minor findings.

nodes.name: Markdown Report Generation
nodes.intent: Generate a human-readable markdown report with summary statistics, severity-grouped tables (missing/misplaced, body mismatch, not deployed), and valid function counts.
constraints: Output: VALIDATION_REPORT.md
Sections: Missing/misplaced, No Match, Outside sql/functions/, Body Mismatch, Not Deployed, Valid

nodes.name: JSON Report Generation
nodes.intent: Generate structured JSON data with timestamp, summary statistics, and per-function results including severity, issues, and details.
constraints: Output: validation_data.json
Must include: timestamp, summary (totals, pass_rate, by_severity), results array

nodes.name: CLI Argument Parsing
nodes.intent: Parse command-line arguments: --output-dir, --verbose, --skip-fallback-search.

nodes.name: Pipeline Execution
nodes.intent: Execute the linear pipeline: discover_all() -> validate each function -> generate_all() reports, with progress output.

nodes.name: Summary and Exit Code
nodes.intent: Print validation summary statistics and return exit code (0 = clean, 1 = issues).

intentlinks.intent: Discovery provides FunctionRecord dict (schema.name -> generated/source parsed data) consumed by Validation for comparison.
Discovery provides FunctionRecord dict to Reporter for source location paths and context in report tables.
Discovery depends on the Parser to extract signatures and bodies from .sql files during both generated cache scanning and source directory scanning.
Validation produces ValidationReport (list of ValidationResult with severity, issues, details) consumed by Reporter to generate output files.
Orchestrator calls FunctionDiscovery.discover_all() to start the pipeline.
Orchestrator iterates through discovered functions and calls FunctionValidator.validate_function() for each.
Orchestrator calls ReportGenerator.generate_all() with results and functions.
Generated cache scanning uses signature extraction to create ParsedFunction objects.
Source scanning uses signature extraction to identify functions in multi-statement files.
Generated cache scanning uses body extraction for each function.
Source scanning uses body extraction for each parsed function.
Type normalization is called during signature extraction to normalize parameter and return types.
Type normalization enables signature comparison by resolving aliases.
Type normalization is used during body comparison for consistent type names.
Existence check results (missing source = CRITICAL, missing DB = WARNING) determine initial severity classification.
Signature mismatch results (language difference = CRITICAL) feed severity assignment.
Body mismatch results (any difference = WARNING with similarity score) feed severity assignment.
Severity-classified results drive the grouping and ordering of the markdown report.
Severity-classified results are serialized into the JSON data structure.
